# inlavanilla

> INLA-style skew-normal marginals for any log-posterior.

If you can write down the log-likelihood plus the log-prior,
[inlavanilla](http://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/) gives you approximate
Bayesian inference for the parameters of your model: posterior marginals
and draws, the marginal likelihood, and leave-one-out cross-validation.
There is no sampler and no tuning, and small models take milliseconds.
It runs the approximation pipeline of
[INLAvaan](https://inlavaan.haziqj.ml/) with nothing model-specific:

1.  a **Laplace approximation** at the posterior mode, with the Laplace
    estimate of the log marginal likelihood;
2.  a **VB mean correction** that recentres the Gaussian at a better
    estimate of the posterior mean;
3.  **skew-normal marginals**, one per parameter, fitted to scans of the
    log-posterior;
4.  **Gaussian copula draws** for any function of the parameters.

Stages 2 and 3 are optional and independent: `vb = FALSE` skips the VB
correction, and `marginals = "gaussian"` keeps the Gaussian marginals
instead of scanning for skew-normal ones. With both, you get the Laplace
approximation alone.

Give [`loo()`](http://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/reference/loo.md) or
[`waic()`](http://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/reference/loo.md) the
log-likelihood as one term per observation, and they estimate the
model’s predictive accuracy from the fit alone, with no refits and no
draws.

The package is pure R and small. Its only dependency outside base R is
[cli](https://cli.r-lib.org/).

## Installation

You can install the development version of inlavanilla from
[GitHub](https://github.com/haziqj/inlavanilla) with:

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("haziqj/inlavanilla")
```

## Example

A trial records 3 responders out of 20 patients. With a uniform prior on
the response rate \\p\\, the posterior is \\\text{Beta}(4, 18)\\:
skewed, and bounded at zero.

[`inla_vanilla()`](http://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/reference/inla_vanilla.md)
works on an unconstrained scale, so we write the log-posterior in terms
of \\\vartheta = \text{logit}(p)\\. The prior is stated for \\p\\, so it
carries the Jacobian \\dp / d\vartheta = p(1 - p)\\:

``` r

library(inlavanilla)

logpost <- function(theta, y, n) {
  p <- plogis(theta[["logit_p"]])
  dbinom(y, n, p, log = TRUE) +
    dbeta(p, 1, 1, log = TRUE) + # prior on p ...
    log(p) + log1p(-p) # ... and the Jacobian
}

fit <- inla_vanilla(logpost, init = c(logit_p = 0), y = 3, n = 20)
#> ✔ Found the posterior mode in 6 iterations [3ms]
#> ✔ VB mean correction, max shift 0.17σ [28ms]
#> ✔ Fitted 1 skew-normal marginal [20ms]
fit
#> ── INLAvanilla ───────────────────────────────────────── Skew-normal + VB ──
#> 
#> Log marginal likelihood: -3.05 · Converged in 6 iterations (55ms)
#> 
#>              Mean     SD    2.5%     50%   97.5%    Mode
#> 1 logit_p  -1.605  0.582  -2.845  -1.569  -0.562  -1.494
```

The summary is on the logit scale.
[`sampling()`](http://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/reference/sampling.md) draws
from the approximate posterior, and its `fun` argument maps each draw
back to \\p\\, or to any other quantity of interest:

``` r

set.seed(1)
p <- sampling(
  fit,
  nsamp = 1e5,
  fun = function(theta) plogis(theta[["logit_p"]])
)
rbind(
  inlavanilla = quantile(p, c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975)),
  exact = qbeta(c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975), 4, 18)
)
#>                   2.5%       50%     97.5%
#> inlavanilla 0.05443460 0.1723549 0.3645844
#> exact       0.05446357 0.1720895 0.3634240
```

The approximation matches the exact posterior, skew included:

``` r

hist(p, breaks = 80, freq = FALSE, border = NA, col = "#F5D0BE",
     main = NULL, xlab = "Response rate p", ylab = NULL, yaxt = "n")
curve(dbeta(x, 4, 18), add = TRUE, lwd = 2, col = "#C2410C")
```

![Histogram of draws of p, skewed to the right, with the exact Beta(4,
18) density overlaid and matching
it.](reference/figures/README-density-1.png)

`summary(fit)` adds diagnostics for each stage of the approximation, and
`plot(fit)` draws the marginals. The [Get
started](http://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/articles/inlavanilla.md) vignette
works through a multi-parameter example: it checks the approximation
against the exact posterior, and covers gradients, derived quantities
and model comparison.

## References

Jamil, H., & Rue, H. (2026a). *Approximate Bayesian inference for
structural equation models using integrated nested Laplace
approximations* (arXiv:2603.25690 \[stat.ME\]). arXiv.
<https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2603.25690>

Jamil, H., & Rue, H. (2026b). *Implementation and workflows for
INLA-based approximate Bayesian structural equation modelling*
(arXiv:2604.00671 \[stat.CO\]). arXiv.
<https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2604.00671>

# Package index

## All functions

- [`diagnostics()`](http://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/reference/diagnostics.md)
  : Diagnostics of an INLAvanilla fit
- [`inla_vanilla()`](http://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/reference/inla_vanilla.md)
  : INLA-style posterior approximation for any log-posterior
- [`loo()`](http://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/reference/loo.md)
  [`waic()`](http://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/reference/loo.md) :
  Leave-one-out cross-validation and WAIC for an INLAvanilla fit
- [`plot(`*`<inla_vanilla>`*`)`](http://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/reference/plot.inla_vanilla.md)
  : Plot an INLAvanilla fit
- [`sampling()`](http://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/reference/sampling.md) :
  Draw from an approximate posterior
- [`summary(`*`<inla_vanilla>`*`)`](http://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/reference/summary.inla_vanilla.md)
  : Summarise an INLAvanilla fit

# Articles

### Get started

- [Get started with
  inlavanilla](http://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/articles/inlavanilla.md):

### Examples

- [Multilevel
  models](http://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/articles/multilevel.md):

  A linear mixed model with the random effects integrated out and drawn
  back afterwards, checked against brms.

- [Diagnostic classification
  models](http://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/articles/dcm.md):

  A DINA model for binary items, with the latent classes summed out,
  checked against Stan.

- [Correlation
  matrices](http://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/articles/correlation.md):

  A multivariate normal with an LKJ prior on its correlation matrix,
  written in terms of canonical partial correlations, checked against
  Stan.

- [Binary factor
  analysis](http://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/articles/binary-cfa.md):

  A one-factor model for binary items, with the factor integrated out by
  Gauss-Hermite quadrature inside the log-posterior.

- [Diagnostic tests without a gold
  standard](http://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/articles/diagnostic-tests.md):

  Three latent class models for five schistosomiasis tests in Ghana,
  with the infection status summed out and a random effect integrated by
  quadrature.

### Articles

- [Diagnostics](http://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/articles/diagnostics.md):

- [Model comparison with LOO and
  WAIC](http://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/articles/model-comparison.md):

- [Speeding up with
  Rcpp](http://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/articles/rcpp.md):

  A structural equation model with 39 parameters, its log-posterior
  written first in R and then in C++ with Rcpp and RcppEigen, with an
  analytic gradient.

- [Gradients and Hessians with
  RTMB](http://haziqj.ml/inlavanilla/articles/rtmb.md):

  The structural equation model of the Rcpp article written for RTMB,
  which differentiates R code automatically to give the gradient and the
  Hessian, and compared with R and C++ for speed and accuracy.
